samples.summary: stampLens' "blanks only, never overwrite" rule makes the per-lens rebuttal partition depend on a model-controlled field, because adjudicateRebuttals never filters rebuttals by lensId
samples.evidence: `adjudicateRebuttals` (scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:1940-1953) is handed the FULL rebuttal list for every lens (`rebuttals` at :2492 is the whole parsed file, :2177-2186) and the ONLY lens partition is `finding.lens`, read inside `matchRebuttal` -> `findingSimilarity` (scripts/agent/rounds.mjs:303). Fresh findings come straight from model output: `FINDING` (review-panel.mjs:79-111) does not set `additionalProperties: false`, and `coerceFindings` (review-panel.mjs:526-536) returns the object unchanged (`return f;`), so a `lens` key emitted by a lens model — e.g. induced by text in the diff under review — survives into `detected`, through `annotateFindings`' `{...f}` copies, and `stampLens` (review-panel.mjs:812-816) deliberately leaves it alone. That finding is then scored against ANOTHER lens's rebuttals and can be overturned by one (`dropped` at :1967, removed from the gate and the summary at :2505-2506). This is exactly the spoofing that prior-findings.mjs:104-106 guards against on the carry-forward path ("`lens` last: a finding cannot spoof its own origin by carrying a `lens` key"); the fresh path now trusts it instead. Before this change fresh findings had no lens and nothing matched, i.e. it failed closed. Fix belongs on the new code: overwrite unconditionally for fresh findings (identity can be preserved by mutating or by only copying when the value actually differs), or strip `lens` in `coerceFindings`, or filter `rebuttals` to `r.lens === lens.id` at review-panel.mjs:2491 so the partition does not rest on model output at all.

samples.summary: A non-string lensId silently stamps every finding of that lens with lens:"", and findings that already carry lens:"" are never stamped at all
samples.evidence: `stampLens` coerces a non-string `lensId` to `""` (review-panel.mjs:813) and skips any finding whose `lens` is already a string, including the empty string (:815). Either case yields findings with `lens: ""`, which `findingSimilarity` (scripts/agent/rounds.mjs:303) can never match against a real rebuttal — the rebuttal reader rejects an empty lens (scripts/agent/rebuttal.mjs:124-126), so the loop silently reverts to the inert behaviour this change exists to fix, with no log line saying so. Fail direction is safe (nothing is overturned), but the failure is invisible; either treat a non-string lens id as a programming error or skip stamping rather than stamping "".

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the repository. stampLens (review-panel.mjs:812-816) preserves an existing string `lens` rather than overwriting it. adjudicateRebuttals (review-panel.mjs:1932-1953) applies no lens filter and is handed the full parsed rebuttal list (built at :2177-2186, passed at :2491-2493), so the ONLY per-lens partition is `finding.lens` as compared in matchRebuttal (rebuttal.mjs:191-194) via findingSimilarity's `trimmed(a.lens) !== trimmed(b.lens)` gate (rounds.mjs:303). The FINDING schema (review-panel.mjs:79-111) declares no `lens` property and does not set additionalProperties:false, and coerceFindings returns well-formed objects unchanged (:534), while clusterFindings/mergeCluster ({...rep}, :664) and annotateFindings ({...f}, :769) copy all keys — so a model-emitted `lens` reaches `merged` at :2480 and survives the stamp. Nothing downstream re-validates lens agreement (isOverturningVerdict rebuttal.mjs:260-271; buildAdjudicatorPrompt :322+ never compares lensId), and an overturn removes the finding from the gate and the summary (:1967, :2505-2506). The contrasting invariant is real and explicit: tagPriorFindings puts `lens` last precisely so a finding cannot spoof its origin (prior-findings.mjs:104-106). The repo's own test asserts the non-overwrite behaviour for a foreign lens (review-panel.test.mjs:3291-3300). This is in the blast-radius lane (a partition invariant enforced in one module and violated in another, plus an unfiltered rebuttal list at an unchanged call site) and is major impact: a genuine blocking finding can be adjudicated against another lens's rebuttal and dropped from the merge gate. No guard makes it unreachable.
